bibl.title: Performance characteristics of five immunoassays for SARS-CoV-2: a head-to-head benchmark comparison

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: FIVE IMMUNOASSAYS MEASURING ONE CONSTRUCT ON ONE SAMPLE SET - 976 pre-pandemic and 536 PCR-confirmed bloods run through four commercial platforms and a novel ELISA, with the thresholds treated as adjustable
span.quote: At the manufacturers' thresholds, for the Abbott assay sensitivity was 92·7% (95% CI 90·2–94·8) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%); for the DiaSorin assay sensitivity was 96·2% (94·2–97·7) and specificity was 98·9% (98·0–99·4); for the Oxford immunoassay sensitivity was 99·1% (97·8–99·7) and specificity was 99·0% (98·1–99·5); for the Roche assay sensitivity was 97·2% (95·4–98·4) and specificity was 99·8% (99·3–100); and for the Siemens assay sensitivity was 98·1% (96·6–99·1) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%).

span.label: how five widely deployed SARS-CoV-2 antibody assays compare when run on identical samples, and what thresholds each needs to reach 98% sensitivity and specificity
span.quote: However, immunoassay performance has not been compared on large, identical sample sets.

span.label: the first head-to-head assessment of four commercial platforms plus a scalable 384-well ELISA on one sample set, with ROC-derived thresholds and an error-rate projection per million tests
span.quote: No published studies assessed all four commercial platforms using the same sample sets.

span.label: method
span.quote: At the manufacturers' thresholds, for the Abbott assay sensitivity was 92·7% (95% CI 90·2–94·8) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%); for the DiaSorin assay sensitivity was 96·2% (94·2–97·7) and specificity was 98·9% (98·0–99·4); for the Oxford immunoassay sensitivity was 99·1% (97·8–99·7) and specificity was 99·0% (98·1–99·5); for the Roche assay sensitivity was 97·2% (95·4–98·4) and specificity was 99·8% (99·3–100); and for the Siemens assay sensitivity was 98·1% (96·6–99·1) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%).

span.label: an instrument's measured accuracy as a property of the cut point somebody chose, in the absence of anything to check the instrument against
span.quote: Notably, no clear gold standard exists against which to assess these antibody tests. RT-PCR positivity is a proxy for the expected presence of antibody, but negative antibody tests in RT-PCR-positive individuals could either reflect antibody test performance, or alternatively be explained by a failure to mount a measurable systemic IgM or IgG antibody response (eg, in cases of immunocompromised individuals), effective infection clearance through other immune mechanisms (eg, T cells), an issue with the sample (eg, a major interferent), or through a false-positive RT-PCR test in individuals who have not had SARS-CoV-2 infection.

span.label: head-to-head benchmark: 976 pre-pandemic and 536 laboratory-confirmed samples through five assays, sensitivity and specificity at the manufacturers' thresholds and at ROC-optimised thresholds
span.term: head-to-head benchmark: 976 pre-pandemic and 536 laboratory-confirmed samples through five assays, sensitivity and specificity at the manufacturers' thresholds and at ROC-optimised thresholds
span.quote: All assays achieved a sensitivity of at least 98% with thresholds optimised to achieve a specificity of at least 98% on samples taken 30 days or more post symptom onset.

span.label: THE PAPER SAYS OUTRIGHT THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO MEASURE THE INSTRUMENTS AGAINST: `Notably, NO CLEAR GOLD STANDARD EXISTS against which to assess these antibody tests. RT-PCR positivity is A PROXY for the expected presence of antibody, but negative antibody tests in RT-PCR-positive individuals COULD EITHER REFLECT ANTIBODY TEST PERFORMANCE, OR ALTERNATIVELY be explained by a failure to mount a measurable systemic IgM or IgG antibody response ... effective infection clearance through other immune mechanisms (eg, T cells), an issue with the sample ... or through A FALSE-POSITIVE RT-PCR TEST`. FIVE WAYS TO GET A DISCORDANT RESULT AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE ASSAY BEING WRONG
span.quote: Notably, no clear gold standard exists against which to assess these antibody tests. RT-PCR positivity is a proxy for the expected presence of antibody, but negative antibody tests in RT-PCR-positive individuals could either reflect antibody test performance, or alternatively be explained by a failure to mount a measurable systemic IgM or IgG antibody response (eg, in cases of immunocompromised individuals), effective infection clearance through other immune mechanisms (eg, T cells), an issue with the sample (eg, a major interferent), or through a false-positive RT-PCR test in individuals who have not had SARS-CoV-2 infection.

span.label: AND THE THRESHOLD IS WHAT MOVES, NOT THE ASSAY: at the manufacturers' cut points the five assays span 92.7% to 99.1% sensitivity, and then `ALL ASSAYS ACHIEVED A SENSITIVITY OF AT LEAST 98% WITH THRESHOLDS OPTIMISED to achieve a specificity of at least 98% on samples taken 30 days or more post symptom onset`. Same five machines, same 1,512 samples, and every one of them passes once someone else chooses the cut point
span.quote: All assays achieved a sensitivity of at least 98% with thresholds optimised to achieve a specificity of at least 98% on samples taken 30 days or more post symptom onset.

span.label: and the authors add the caveat that makes it honest rather than circular: `opportunities to optimise sensitivity for the Abbott, DiaSorin, and Roche assays THROUGH CHANGES TO THRESHOLDS AND SAMPLE TIMING, although ANY POST-HOC CHANGES TO THRESHOLDS WOULD REQUIRE REPEAT VERIFICATION of sensitivity and specificity`
span.quote: In conclusion, we characterised the performance of four commercial antibody platforms and a new ELISA from an academic research facility, all of which achieved the desired specificity, and with opportunities to optimise sensitivity for the Abbott, DiaSorin, and Roche assays through changes to thresholds and sample timing, although any post-hoc changes to thresholds would require repeat verification of sensitivity and specificity.

span.label: AND THE COST OF THE CHOICE IS COUNTED IN PEOPLE: `at a 10% seroprevalence, the Siemens assay would generate an estimated 2800 TOTAL ERRORS PER MILLION TESTS, versus the DiaSorin assay at a rate of 13 700 TOTAL ERRORS PER MILLION TESTS`. A five-fold difference in wrong answers, from a choice of platform
span.quote: However, differences observed in assay performance translate into thousands of additional incorrect diagnoses between the worst and best platforms if millions of tests are done in large populations. For example, at a 10% seroprevalence, the Siemens assay would generate an estimated 2800 total errors per million tests, versus the DiaSorin assay at a rate of 13 700 total errors per million tests.

span.label: AND THE PRIOR LITERATURE HAS THE RIFLE PROBLEM: `For the Abbott assay, sensitivity RANGED FROM 93.4% TO 100% ... (70 to 680 samples) ... for the DiaSorin assay, we found A SINGLE SENSITIVITY ESTIMATE OF 94.4% ... (18 SAMPLES)`, and `NO PUBLISHED STUDIES ASSESSED ALL FOUR COMMERCIAL PLATFORMS USING THE SAME SAMPLE SETS`. The spread was never a property of the assays
span.quote: For the Abbott assay, sensitivity ranged from 93·4% to 100% for samples taken at least 14 days post symptom onset (70 to 680 samples) and specificity from 95·1% to 100% (nine to 1020); for the DiaSorin assay, we found a single sensitivity estimate of 94·4% on samples taken at least 14 days post symptom onset (18 samples) and specificity ranged from 94·9% to 100% (69 to 1140 samples).

span.label: ONE INSTRUMENT WAS DROPPED FROM THE COMPARISON BEFORE IT BEGAN, ON THE STRENGTH OF A PRIOR REPORT: `the sensitivity of the EUROIMMUN assay HAS BEEN REPORTED AS BEING APPROXIMATELY 90%. WE THEREFORE REPLACED THIS with the SARS-CoV-2 Total assay (Siemens ...)`. A selection decision that shapes what the benchmark can find, made in the open and worth reading next to the finding that prior estimates ranged from 93.4% to 100% on samples as small as eighteen
span.quote: However, the sensitivity of the EUROIMMUN assay has been reported as being approximately 90%. We therefore replaced this with the SARS-CoV-2 Total assay (Siemens, Munich, Germany) in a head-to-head comparison.

span.label: AND THE ASSESSMENT CRITERIA THEMSELVES HAD BEEN RELAXED: `governments, regulators, and clinical laboratories have had to BALANCE THE URGENT NEED ... WITH THE FEW DATA AVAILABLE on assay performance, LEADING TO A RELAXATION OF TYPICAL ASSESSMENT CRITERIA (eg, the US Food and Drug Administration's [FDA] EMERGENCY USE AUTHORIZATION programme)`
span.quote: To date, few thorough, direct assessments of immunoassay performance on large sample sets have been done, and governments, regulators, and clinical laboratories have had to balance the urgent need to facilitate the demand for serological testing with the few data available on assay performance, leading to a relaxation of typical assessment criteria (eg, the US Food and Drug Administration's [FDA] Emergency Use Authorization programme).

span.label: AND THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON WHAT THE TEST IS FOR: `The optimal deployment of assays SHOULD REFLECT USE CASE - eg, an optimised assay measuring antibodies to NUCLEOCAPSID protein might be most relevant for disease surveillance IN THE CONTEXT OF A WIDESPREAD ROLLOUT OF VACCINES, WHICH ARE MOSTLY SPIKE-PROTEIN BASED`. The best instrument changes when the population changes
span.quote: The optimal deployment of assays should reflect use case—eg, an optimised assay measuring antibodies to nucleocapsid protein might be most relevant for disease surveillance in the context of a widespread rollout of vaccines, which are mostly spike-protein based.

span.label: and the headline metrics are not the useful ones: `Although SENSITIVITY AND SPECIFICITY ARE IMPORTANT, estimating the NEGATIVE AND POSITIVE PREDICTIVE VALUES of each assay are PERHAPS MORE USEFUL in deciding how tests can best be used and interpreted` - because those depend on prevalence, which is what the assays are being used to estimate
span.quote: Although sensitivity and specificity are important, estimating the negative and positive predictive values of each assay are perhaps more useful in deciding how tests can best be used and interpreted.

span.label: WHO IS NOT IN THE SAMPLE, STATED: `Our sample sets MIGHT UNDER-REPRESENT SOME ETHNIC GROUPS, DID NOT INCLUDE CHILDREN, and captured INSUFFICIENT CLINICAL META-DATA to characterise features (eg, being immunocompromised), WHICH MIGHT EXPLAIN THE PRESENCE OF FALSE-NEGATIVE ANTIBODY RESULTS in individuals with RT-PCR-confirmed infection`
span.quote: Our sample sets might under-represent some ethnic groups, did not include children, and captured insufficient clinical meta-data to characterise features (eg, being immunocompromised), which might explain the presence of false-negative antibody results in individuals with RT-PCR-confirmed infection.

span.label: and three discordant samples are left explicitly undecided rather than counted as failures: `The three samples that were negative by all assays in our study COULD PLAUSIBLY HAVE HAD A BIOLOGICAL ABSENCE OF ANTIBODIES`
span.quote: The three samples that were negative by all assays in our study could plausibly have had a biological absence of antibodies.

span.label: THE PUBLISHED RECORD OF THIS PAPER CARRIES ITS OWN CORRECTION: `This online publication HAS BEEN CORRECTED. The corrected version first appeared at thelancet.com/infection on NOVEMBER 25, 2020`, and the PMC record we staged is VERSION 2. Q-714's distinction applies - a correction re-grounds a record, it does not retire it
span.quote: This online publication has been corrected. The corrected version first appeared at thelancet.com/infection on November 25, 2020

span.quote: In conclusion, we characterised the performance of four commercial antibody platforms and a new ELISA from an academic research facility, all of which achieved the desired specificity, and with opportunities to optimise sensitivity for the Abbott, DiaSorin, and Roche assays through changes to thresholds and sample timing, although any post-hoc changes to thresholds would require repeat verification of sensitivity and specificity.

span.quote: For the Abbott assay, sensitivity ranged from 93·4% to 100% for samples taken at least 14 days post symptom onset (70 to 680 samples) and specificity from 95·1% to 100% (nine to 1020); for the DiaSorin assay, we found a single sensitivity estimate of 94·4% on samples taken at least 14 days post symptom onset (18 samples) and specificity ranged from 94·9% to 100% (69 to 1140 samples).

span.quote: However, the sensitivity of the EUROIMMUN assay has been reported as being approximately 90%. We therefore replaced this with the SARS-CoV-2 Total assay (Siemens, Munich, Germany) in a head-to-head comparison.

span.term: AND THE ASSESSMENT CRITERIA THEMSELVES HAD BEEN RELAXED: `LEADING TO A RELAXATION OF TYPICAL ASSESSMENT CRITERIA (eg, the US Food and Drug Administration's [FDA] EMERGENCY USE AUTHORIZATION programme)`
span.quote: To date, few thorough, direct assessments of immunoassay performance on large sample sets have been done, and governments, regulators, and clinical laboratories have had to balance the urgent need to facilitate the demand for serological testing with the few data available on assay performance, leading to a relaxation of typical assessment criteria (eg, the US Food and Drug Administration's [FDA] Emergency Use Authorization programme).

span.label: THE BEST INSTRUMENT CHANGES WHEN THE POPULATION DOES: `an optimised assay measuring antibodies to NUCLEOCAPSID protein might be most relevant for disease surveillance IN THE CONTEXT OF A WIDESPREAD ROLLOUT OF VACCINES, WHICH ARE MOSTLY SPIKE-PROTEIN BASED`
span.term: THE BEST INSTRUMENT CHANGES WHEN THE POPULATION DOES: `an optimised assay measuring antibodies to NUCLEOCAPSID protein might be most relevant for disease surveillance IN THE CONTEXT OF A WIDESPREAD ROLLOUT OF VACCINES, WHICH ARE MOSTLY SPIKE-PROTEIN BASED`
span.quote: The optimal deployment of assays should reflect use case—eg, an optimised assay measuring antibodies to nucleocapsid protein might be most relevant for disease surveillance in the context of a widespread rollout of vaccines, which are mostly spike-protein based.

span.quote: Our sample sets might under-represent some ethnic groups, did not include children, and captured insufficient clinical meta-data to characterise features (eg, being immunocompromised), which might explain the presence of false-negative antibody results in individuals with RT-PCR-confirmed infection.

span.label: `NO CLEAR GOLD STANDARD EXISTS against which to assess these antibody tests` - the substitute is `RT-PCR positivity ... A PROXY for the expected presence of antibody`
span.term: gold standard
span.quote: Notably, no clear gold standard exists against which to assess these antibody tests. RT-PCR positivity is a proxy for the expected presence of antibody, but negative antibody tests in RT-PCR-positive individuals could either reflect antibody test performance, or alternatively be explained by a failure to mount a measurable systemic IgM or IgG antibody response (eg, in cases of immunocompromised individuals), effective infection clearance through other immune mechanisms (eg, T cells), an issue with the sample (eg, a major interferent), or through a false-positive RT-PCR test in individuals who have not had SARS-CoV-2 infection.

span.label: 98 — the sensitivity and specificity every one of the five assays reaches once the threshold is chosen for it rather than by the manufacturer
span.quote: All assays achieved a sensitivity of at least 98% with thresholds optimised to achieve a specificity of at least 98% on samples taken 30 days or more post symptom onset.

span.label: the Abbott assay's sensitivity at the manufacturer's threshold - the lowest of the five, and above 98% once the threshold is moved
span.quote: At the manufacturers' thresholds, for the Abbott assay sensitivity was 92·7% (95% CI 90·2–94·8) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%); for the DiaSorin assay sensitivity was 96·2% (94·2–97·7) and specificity was 98·9% (98·0–99·4); for the Oxford immunoassay sensitivity was 99·1% (97·8–99·7) and specificity was 99·0% (98·1–99·5); for the Roche assay sensitivity was 97·2% (95·4–98·4) and specificity was 99·8% (99·3–100); and for the Siemens assay sensitivity was 98·1% (96·6–99·1) and specificity was 99·9% (99·4–100%).

span.label: the proxy standing in for an absent gold standard, with four named ways it can disagree with an antibody result without either being wrong
span.term: RT-PCR positivity
span.quote: Notably, no clear gold standard exists against which to assess these antibody tests. RT-PCR positivity is a proxy for the expected presence of antibody, but negative antibody tests in RT-PCR-positive individuals could either reflect antibody test performance, or alternatively be explained by a failure to mount a measurable systemic IgM or IgG antibody response (eg, in cases of immunocompromised individuals), effective infection clearance through other immune mechanisms (eg, T cells), an issue with the sample (eg, a major interferent), or through a false-positive RT-PCR test in individuals who have not had SARS-CoV-2 infection.
